transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-30
Time: 15:00-15:54 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyer (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Aisha Khan (Blueforge VP Eng), Marco Ruiz (Blueforge Platform Lead), Lena Cho (Blueforge SRE), Diego Tran (Blueforge Data Eng)

Summary:
Quick Q3 townhall focused on recent availability incidents, rising token costs tied to a new feature roll-out, and options for Dedicated burst capacity and on-prem/private deployment considerations. Agreed to run focused benchmarks and share a pricing breakdown. Next steps captured as action items.

Topics:
- Incident postmortem recap (latency spikes + fallback paths)
- Usage and cost drivers (feature X rollout + more long-tail requests)
- Capacity options: Dedicated burst, Private/VPC, caching/batching knobs
- Roadmap alignment: upcoming model upgrades and canary rollout
- Security/compliance reminders for audit logs and retention

Action items: see metadata list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Meyer: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this as a townhall — quick updates, very practical items. Aisha, you want to kick off with how Q3 looked from your side?
[00:12] Aisha Khan: yeah thanks Jordan. so q3 overall adoption looks good, we hit the v2 of the recommendation feature, but we had a few reliability blips in late August, there was a 15–20 minute window where 95th and 99th spiked, customers saw some timeouts.
[00:28] Marco Ruiz: right, the new feature increased tail latency because of a higher average sequence length and a lot of small requests that bypassed caching. also we saw a cost increase on tokens that we didn't expect, Diego has the exact numbers.
[00:42] Diego Tran: yeah sorry, rough numbers — token consumption up ~34% month-on-month for the recommender endpoint, 60% of that was from long prompts in the profile enrichment flow. some of the spikes aligned with batch jobs running at 02:00 UTC.
[00:55] Priya Desai: ok that explains a lot — sounds like two contributors: sequence length distribution and some background jobs. For the reliability blip did you see fallback events to smaller model variants or error rates?
[01:10] Lena Cho: we did see the fallback trigger once, actually the route policy pushed to a lower-capacity model and then things recovered but with reduced quality. the tracing is a bit coarse right now, i'll send exact traces.
[01:23] Jordan Meyer: thanks, yes that fallback is working as intended but ideally we'd avoid hitting it. couple things we can help with: batching and prefix/KV caching to reduce repetition, and a targeted canary for the recommender where we pin a quantized variant.
[01:40] Aisha Khan: quick question — send us the economics: if we batch more aggressively what's the expected cost delta and latency tradeoff? we need numbers we can show execs.
[01:52] Jordan Meyer: absolutely, we can run a cost/latency matrix. Priya, can you capture a baseline and then a few tuning permutations?
[01:58] Priya Desai: yes i'll do that, i'll include per-token cost, expected throughput changes, and 99th latency impact. note: if we push batching too much it can increase single-request latency, so we'll show that sweet spot.
[02:12] Marco Ruiz: also we're considering Dedicated burst capacity — we like predictable throughput but not sure on commit sizes. what are typical commit tiers?
[02:23] Samir Patel: typical reserved tiers start at the X GPU pool equivalent, but we can model a configuration with burst buckets. Jordan can send examples of commit vs burst economics.
[02:34] Jordan Meyer: i'll include Dedicated configs plus a comparison to hosted with heavier caching. we'll also show a hybrid: keep hosted for baseline, offload heavy enrichment to Dedicated during peak windows.
[02:47] Diego Tran: on the security side, execs asked about audit logs and retention for two of our customers who need 7-year retention — can Redwood support that in Private?
[02:58] Jordan Meyer: yes Private/VPC or on-prem supports long-term retention and customer-managed KMS. for hosted we have limited retention defaults but enterprise add-ons are available. i'll attach the compliance whitepaper.
[03:12] Aisha Khan: good. one thing the team is worried about is the canary rollout — last time the model drifted and produced low-quality outputs after an automatic fallback. is there a way to run canaries with a higher-quality guardrail?
[03:25] Priya Desai: yes, we recommend staged rollouts with evaluation sets — Redwood Optimize can score outputs and flag regressions. we can configure automatic rollback thresholds and a manual review hook.
[03:36] Marco Ruiz: we would want a human review for novel cohorts. also is there an easy way to compare a quantized variant in terms of perf/quality?
[03:46] Priya Desai: we do A/B tests with metric tracking. quantization profiles are included in the profile recommendations; i'll run an internal micro-benchmark showing perplexity and latency differences.
[03:58] Lena Cho: related to the outage, we have three sample traces — i'll attach them. also, our SREs want a recommended KV cache TTL pattern — the default is not tailored.
[04:09] Jordan Meyer: great please share those traces. on TTLs, Priya will put recommended ranges based on access patterns and profile. we also suggest a small Redis tier for hot prefixes.
[04:21] Diego Tran: while we're on the topic of caching — any guidance on prefix-aware caching vs whole-request caches? we saw cache churn with small variations in user inputs.
[04:33] Priya Desai: prefix/KV caching is better for completion-style workloads; for classification or short prompts whole-request caching can be effective. also normalizing inputs reduces churn. we'll include a doc link.
[04:45] Aisha Khan: thanks. on costs — we saw a line-item for experimental embeddings we didn't expect, are those billable by default?
[04:56] Jordan Meyer: embeddings are separate units on the invoice, sometimes experiments default to higher dimensional models. we'll audit your model selections and suggest smaller embedding models where acceptable.
[05:06] Marco Ruiz: can you also help with a forecast for Q4 if we proceed with the feature expansion? exec wants a 3-month burn forecast.
[05:16] Samir Patel: yes we can produce a forecast with low/medium/high usage bands. include seasonal jobs and planned rollouts.
[05:24] Aisha Khan: ok good. switching to reliability: Lena, can you summarize the postmortem so we are all aligned?
[05:31] Lena Cho: sure, root cause was twofold: a background enrichment job overlapped peak traffic and a small fraction of requests bypassed the cache due to a header mismatch. we had insufficient trace sampling so detection lagged. we added a fix to normalize headers and increased trace sampling from 0.5% to 5% for the recommender route.
[05:52] Priya Desai: that header mismatch is a classic — quick win then. we can also recommend request signature normalization, and small batching on the service side for micro-requests.
[06:05] Aisha Khan: what's the expected SLO delta if we adopt these suggestions?
[06:11] Jordan Meyer: conservative estimate: 99th latency improvement of 20–30% for the recommender, and token cost reduction around 10–18% depending on sequence length normalization. we'll validate with a benchmark.
[06:24] Marco Ruiz: question — is it worth moving that enrichment workload to Private/on-prem altogether? we have compliance drivers and would get data locality.
[06:33] Jordan Meyer: yes Private gives more control — KMS, audit log retention, and dedicated networking. tradeoff is operational ownership and initial platform setup. Redwood can support an on-prem package and we have partners for install.
[06:47] Diego Tran: any typical time-to-live for on-prem migrations? we have a Nov compliance audit so time is sensitive.
[06:55] Samir Patel: an on-prem pilot can be done in 6–10 weeks depending on cluster readiness. for VPC-private it's faster because we manage the plane and you keep data in your VPC.
[07:08] Aisha Khan: that's in line with our timeline. we might start with Dedicated for burst in Oct then evaluate Private for the sensitive workloads.
[07:18] Jordan Meyer: good plan. we'll draft a proposed phased approach in the follow-up.
[07:24] Marco Ruiz: another topic — SLA for high-volume customers; what availability figures can we expect with Dedicated?
[07:33] Jordan Meyer: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency objectives (we'll send the exact SLA terms). practical uptime for most setups is 99.95% with multi-zone, but your commitment size and network topology affect that.
[07:46] Priya Desai: and we can enable graceful degradation policies so non-critical routes fall back before critical ones do.
[07:54] Lena Cho: can we get a per-route cost and latency breakdown in Console? that's useful for chargeback.
[08:01] Samir Patel: yes Console has token-level breakdown and per-route dashboards. Jordan will include screenshots in the follow-up.
[08:09] Aisha Khan: on governance, we need RBAC that maps to our internal roles, SSO + SCIM, and audit trails. does Redwood provide SCIM and SAML?
[08:19] Jordan Meyer: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, role-based access controls, and audit logs for admin actions. for hosted customers there are admin audit logs; for Private you can push logs to your SIEM.
[08:30] Diego Tran: perfect. any compliance certs relevant? ISO, SOC2?
[08:34] Jordan Meyer: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and pursuing ISO; i'll attach the latest attestation.
[08:42] Marco Ruiz: competitor note — we've evaluated DeepServe and CloudPrompt. DeepServe had better latency in small-scale tests but worse horizontal scaling. thought I'd flag that.
[08:53] Jordan Meyer: good to know. we'll make sure our benchmark covers scale.
[08:58] Aisha Khan: back to actionables — we'll need a clear pilot success criteria. for us: under 200ms P50, under 450ms P99 for recommender, and under 8% token cost delta vs baseline.
[09:12] Jordan Meyer: great, we'll draft measurable success criteria and include them in the pilot doc.
[09:19] Priya Desai: i'll coordinate the benchmark and include perf/perplexity tradeoffs for quantized vs full precision.
[09:26] Lena Cho: i'll provide the traces and the job schedule that overlapped the outage.
[09:31] Diego Tran: also we'll try one week of reduced background job cadence to test impact.
[09:37] Marco Ruiz: timeline-wise, can we see a draft pilot plan by next Tuesday?
[09:41] Jordan Meyer: yes — Jordan will share an initial plan by 2026-10-05.
[09:46] Samir Patel: and we'll include an estimate for Dedicated commit tiers and an example billing comparison.
[09:51] Aisha Khan: any blockers from Redwood on doing the micro-benchmarks?
[09:55] Priya Desai: nope, we just need the sample traces, and a short list of endpoints and request payload examples. the team will run them in our staging env.
[10:05] Jordan Meyer: ok team — final recap: send traces, get baseline, run batching/cache permutations, produce cost/latency matrix, draft pilot + SLA language, and evaluate Dedicated vs Private timelines.
[10:18] Aisha Khan: perfect, thanks everyone. appreciated the rapid troubleshooting on the outage.
[10:24] Marco Ruiz: thanks all.
[10:29] (meeting closed)
